prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Mixed · Multilingual glossary (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "English" · longest unbreakable word 76px · one-line width 165px
  col 2: header "中文" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 62px
  col 3: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 107px
  col 4: header "한국어" · longest unbreakable word 13px · one-line width 73px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 112px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A five-language glossary for translators/writers: one English source term per row, with parallel translations in Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic. Its job is lookup and cross-language comparison, not numeric analysis.","reading":"The eye anchors on the English column (col 1) to find the term, then sweeps right across the four translation columns, comparing the same row across scripts. Rows must read as units, so no column may be so narrow that a row becomes a ragged multi-line tower while its neighbours are one line.","groups":["cols 2–5 (中文, 日本語, 한국어, العربية) form one parallel group of equal-role translation columns; they should share a common rhythm even though their scripts differ in width","col 1 (English) is the anchor/key column and should be visually dominant over the translations"],"keep_intact":["Arabic words in col 5, especially the 44px unbreakable token — col 5 must get at least ~65px so no Arabic word splits mid-word","English words in col 1 (longest unbreakable 76px) — col 1 must stay ≥ ~97px so 'Horizontal' never breaks","All CJK single terms (表格, 表, 표) which are short and must not be split into stray characters by over-narrow columns"],"may_wrap":["Multi-word English phrases ('Horizontal scrolling', 'Column width allocation') — natural wrap at the space, absorbed by existing row height","Japanese and Chinese terms (横スクロール, 横向滚动, 列幅の割り当て) — these wrap cleanly at character boundaries","Korean phrases (가로 스크롤, 열 너비 할당) — wrap at the space between eojeol","Arabic phrases — wrap at word boundaries as long as each word fits"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [100, 55, 70, 60, 74] · table 360×335px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [104, 54, 70, 60, 71] · table 360×335px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [98, 53, 69, 60, 79] · table 360×335px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"The English anchor column at 100px is right: the 76px word 'Horizontal' never splits and the long phrases wrap only at spaces ('Horizontal / scrolling', 'Column width / allocation'), so the key column reads cleanly. Arabic at 74px has real slack (44px words plus room), so no Arabic word ever breaks. All five headers stay on one line.","problems":"Korean is the broken column: at 60px (39px of text) '열 너비 할당' fragments into '열 너 / 비 할 / 당' and '줄바꿈' leaves a dangling '꿈', so a row that should read as one unit becomes a three-line tower. Chinese at 55px (34px) splits '可读性' into '可读 / 性', an orphan character on its own line. Meanwhile Arabic, whose content is not the longest, is the widest translation column, so ~9px of pure slack sits there while Korean starves.","cause":"Width is allocated inversely to need: 74px to Arabic (needs only 65) and 60px to Korean (needs ~65–66 to keep '열 너비' whole and '스크롤' intact), plus 55px to Chinese where 3-character terms need ~47px of text (68px column) to stay on one line."},{"design":"r1B","good":"English at 104px is unassailable — no risk of a mid-word split and the phrase wrapping stays natural. Arabic at 71px is still comfortable. Headers all one line, no mid-word splits, rows 1–2 compact at 36px.","problems":"This is r1A with the fix applied to the wrong column: English gained 4px of slack it does not need, while Chinese lost 1px and Korean was left at 60. The '可读 / 性' orphan in Chinese is now the most conspicuous defect in the table and the Korean three-fragment tower is unchanged. Arabic is still over-provisioned relative to its content.","cause":"Taking width from Chinese (55→54, text 33px) to fund English dominance (100→104) — English only needs 97–98 to hold its 76px word, so those pixels are wasted while two translation columns stay below their wrap thresholds (Chinese ~68, Korean ~65)."},{"design":"r1C","good":"Arabic at 79px (58px of text) is the most comfortable of the three: 'سهولة القراءة' and 'توزيع عرض الأعمدة' break into genuinely balanced short lines and the RTL column reads smoothly. English at 98px still holds its longest word intact, and headers remain on one line.","problems":"Chinese at 53px (32px of text) is the narrowest column in the table and produces the worst orphan: '可读 / 性' with a single character alone. Korean is still 60px, so the three-fragment '열 너 / 비 할 / 당' persists. Worse, the parallel group now has no rhythm at all — 53 / 69 / 60 / 79 — so four columns that play the same role look like four unrelated columns, and the eye cannot sweep a row evenly.","cause":"All available slack was pushed into Arabic (79px, ~14px beyond what the 44px words need), while Chinese was squeezed to its minimum; the group's width spread (26px) exceeds the actual content differences between the scripts."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"floors-met","widths":[98,67,64,65,65],"change":"Set every column at or just above its wrap threshold instead of one column hogging slack: English 98 (text 77 ≥ 76px word), Chinese 67 (text 46, so '可读性' finally holds one line), Korean 65 (text 44, enough for '열 너비' whole and '스크롤' intact), Arabic 65 (exactly the 44px word + safety). Japanese pays at 64, so '列幅の割り当て' goes to four short lines and row 6 grows — the table gets ~15px taller, but no cell contains a mid-word split or a stray fragment in Korean/Arabic."},{"name":"japanese-first","widths":[98,62,68,66,65],"change":"Buy back the row-6 height by giving Japanese 68px (text 47) — three characters per line instead of two, so '横スクロール' becomes 3+2 and '列幅の割り当て' 3+3+1, keeping row 6 at three lines and the table at 335px. Korean 66 is fully clean, Arabic 65 keeps its words whole. The price is Chinese back at 62 (text 41), so '可读性' again breaks 2+1 — I accept one orphan in row 3 to avoid a four-line row 6 and to restore a steadier group rhythm (62/68/66/65)."},{"name":"uniform-parallel","widths":[98,65,65,66,65],"change":"A new idea: treat cols 2–5 as a true parallel group and give them near-equal widths (65/65/66/65) so the translation band scans as one rhythm, with only English dominant at 98. Korean (66) is clean and Arabic (65) is safe, but Chinese and Japanese both sit at text 44 — just under the ~46px three-character threshold — so '可读性' and '可読性' both wrap 2+1 and Japanese falls to two characters per line (row 6 four lines). Choose this if visual evenness of the translation band matters more than eliminating the two three-character orphans."}]}
